svg.text: Hold the pool mean exactly fixed, move the variation between prompts,
and the selection gap collapses from 0.10 to 0.03
The judge only ever compares candidates written for the same prompt. Variation parked between prompts is
invisible to it, so it cannot become a selection gap.
323 logged rounds of 12 prompts each. The logged candidates are re-arranged into sub-pools of 4 per prompt with the top 2 kept, scored by
the judges' own recorded scores. Selection only — nothing is retrained.
A. The same candidates, arranged two ways at one pool mean
Arrangement 1: every prompt
is split, so the judge
always has a choice
Arrangement 2: prompts are
all-or-nothing, so there is
nothing to choose
12 prompts, 4 candidates each
12 prompts, 4 candidates each
scores 1 (chose the risky gamble)
scores 0
The two grids are an illustration of the re-arrangement at pool mean 0.50; the real
arrangements are solved round by round from logged candidates and are less extreme.
Identical pool mean, exact by construction: 24 of the 48 candidates score
1 on both sides above, and across all 323 rounds the largest difference in
pool mean between the two arrangements is 0.000000.
Measured over all 323 rounds:
arrangement 1
arrangement 2
within-prompt spread
average over prompts of the standard deviation of that prompt's 4
candidate scores
between-prompt variance
variance across prompts of each prompt's own mean candidate score
size of the selection gap
kept-candidate mean minus pool mean, size ignoring sign, averaged over
rounds
one shared scale
traded off
The trade-off that makes this possible: variation taken out of the prompts does
not vanish, it reappears between them. The pool mean never moves.
Round by round, arrangement 1 gave the larger selection gap in 239 of the 323 rounds,
tied in 71, and gave a smaller one in 13.
B. Both arrangements obey the same law
Each mark is one round under one arrangement. Judge agreement is the
correlation, inside a single prompt, between the judge's score and the
value score, averaged over prompts.
judge agreement × within-prompt spread
selection gap (kept mean minus pool mean)
arrangement 1 — reaches far out along the line
arrangement 2 — packed into the shaded band
gap = 0.86 × (agreement × spread) − 0.005
one line, both arrangements: r = 0.93 over 646 arrangement-rounds
fitted apart: slope 0.85 for arrangement 1, 0.83 for arrangement 2
One line fits both arrangements. Re-arranging the candidates does
not change the rule that turns spread into a selection gap; it
changes how much spread the judge is shown. Pool means across
these rounds run from 0.10 to 0.96, and each round's two marks sit
at the same pool mean as each other.
